presentation_summary: 43-year-old man presented with three days of severe right lower quadrant abdominal pain.
Symptoms included anorexia, fever, and nausea without vomiting.
Exam showed right lower quadrant rebound tenderness.
Laboratory testing showed leukocytosis of 19.8 x10^9/L with neutrophilia.
CT showed a normal appendix, multiple right-sided colonic diverticula, adjacent inflammatory fat stranding, and locules of free gas consistent with isolated stage 1 acute cecal diverticulitis.

white blood cell count was 19.8 x 10^9/L

imaging.finding: Inflammatory fat stranding adjacent to the cecal diverticula.
Locules of free gas adjacent to the involved cecum.

confirmatory_findings.finding: Paper final diagnosis of isolated Hinchey stage 1 acute cecal diverticulitis
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: isolated Hinchey stage 1 acute cecal diverticulitis

confirmatory_findings.finding: Clinical resolution after intravenous antibiotics and rehydration
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: medical management with intravenous antibiotics and rehydration

quality_warnings: Final diagnosis, conservative-treatment response, and follow-up colonoscopy are non-ranking evidence.
Normal appendix is retained as pre-treatment imaging evidence because it is a presentation CT finding, not a final adjudication label.
